human_tolerance.notes: Found in parks and backyards with suitable shrubbery, and eats garden produce; feeds on the ground, so it is drawn to ground-spread feed.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Eggs are laid from March; the breeding season runs from early April to early August, with 2-3 broods a year. The window is an approximation of the Wikipedia dates.

vocalizations.description: A long repeating series of notes ended with a trill, sung from a low perch.
A single-note call, heard as seet, tseek, tsip, cheet or cheenk, given when a threat is near.

common_names.note: English name 'California towhee' from Wikidata and Wikipedia.

range.note: Native to coastal western Oregon and California (US) and Baja California and Baja California Sur (MX), per Wikipedia introduction. Presence in the US is a native-range claim. Not introduced.

range.koppen.note: Authored mapping from Wikipedia habitat text (chaparral, brush, open woodland, desert slopes, Mediterranean coast) to Csa, Csb and BSk. No Koppen source was consulted.

traits.body_plan.note: Passerine bird: Vertebrate, biped_winged, two walking limbs, feathered, endothermic (standard for birds; GBIF class Aves).

traits.mass_kg.note: 0.0528 kg = 52.83 g, the Dryad 'mass' value for row X=228, read as grams and converted to kg. It lies within the Wikipedia sex averages (53.9 g males, 51.8 g females).

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Wikipedia: males 48.6-61.2 g, females 46.3-61.2 g. The combined range 46.3-61.2 g is converted to kg.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 20-25 cm (and 21-25 cm) length, 0.225 m. Nose or beak tip to tail tip is assumed to match the Wikipedia overall length.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Wikipedia: wingspan about 11.4 in (29 cm), converted to 0.29 m.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Derived, not a published lifespan. Input: annual adult survival S = 0.636 (Dryad X=228, MAPS, 15-year mark-recapture, United States). Assumption: constant annual adult survival with no age structure. Mean adult lifetime = -1 / ln(S) = 2.2 years. Limitations: this excludes first-year mortality, so it overstates the typical lifespan of a fledgling, and it is not a maximum or captive value. Low confidence: a single study row, and the species is not verified against a longevity record. The field asks for typical wild lifespan; this is the closest defensible proxy.

traits.diet.note: Authored allocation. Wikipedia names seeds, grasses and herbs as the main food; insects, snails, millipedes and spiders in the breeding season; garden produce (apricots, plums, peas). The 0.6/0.2/0.1/0.1 split is authored, not measured.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia: most often seen travelling or feeding singly or in pairs; keeps contact with its mate, perhaps forming lifelong pairs.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Diurnal inferred from Wikipedia's descriptions of daytime ground foraging and singing. No source gives a time-of-day statement directly.

traits.defense.note: Flees into shrubbery (Wikipedia: 'they tend to hide in shrubbery'); runs rapidly for short distances.

traits.wariness.note: Authored judgement: moderately wary, but adapted to suburban parks and gardens (Wikipedia).

traits.nest_type.note: Bulky cup nest in low branches or shrubs 0.5-4 m above ground (Wikipedia, Nesting).

habitat.use.note: Authored split: ground foraging and low shrub perching, with brief aerial moves. Wikipedia describes ground foraging and perching in low scrub.

habitat.resources.note: Weights are authored. Seed and invertebrate months follow Wikipedia's 'during breeding season' (approximated as March to August). Garden fruit has no month limit in the source.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Adapter: Wikipedia describes parks, lowland towns and backyards with appropriate shrubbery.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: non-migratory; pairs remain together, active year-round.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding window 03-01 to 08-31 covers March egg laying through early August. It is an approximation of the Wikipedia dates (eggs March to September, breeding early April to early August).

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg duration 12.5 days is the midpoint of Wikipedia's 11-14 day incubation. The juvenile scale 0.8 is authored, not sourced.

vocalizations.song.note: Wikipedia: 'the song consists of a long repeating series ended with a trill'. Time windows and months are authored to match the shared program, which sings only when the sun is between -6 and 12 degrees (dawn and dusk); midday song that real birds give is not modelled. Season months are empty (all year) with no source.

vocalizations.alarm.note: Wikipedia describes a single-note call (seet, tseek, tsip, cheet, cheenk, peenk) without naming its function. The alarm context is authored.

look.note: Authored block mesh: brown body, buff belly, dark-streaked head and rust undertail, matching Wikipedia's 'dull brown overall with light rust undertail covert feathers and buff or rust-colored streaks at the throat'. Proportions are judgement.

behavior.note: Shared bt-perching-songbird-v1 program. Feeding uses food_tag 'seed' (the main diet item). Nest-building months 3 to 6 are the program's explicit month set, which is a partial cover of Wikipedia's March to early August breeding window. Limitations are listed in the PR body.

traits.limb_count.note: Passerine bird: two walking limbs (legs); wings are not counted, per the schema convention.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Hop for ground foraging ('lunging forward and hopping backwards') and fly for short moves and flight to perch (Wikipedia; program actions). Walk is not declared because the shared program does not use it.

traits.flight.note: Powered flight: Wikipedia describes short flights; it is a passerine, so powered flight is the standard form.

traits.metamorphosis.note: None; altricial young hatch and grow without metamorphosis.

traits.perching.note: Perches in low branches and shrubs; Wikipedia describes nests in low branches or shrubs and perching in low scrub.

traits.size_class.note: Small (mass below 1 kg, per the schema's size class rule), from traits.mass_kg.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Shrub thicket: Wikipedia says towhees hide in shrubbery and are found in shrubs.
